countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

universities.name: Marwadi University
universities.summary: Marwadi University is a state private university in Rajkot, Gujarat, established under the Gujarat Private Universities Act No. 9 of 2016 and promoted by the Marwadi Chandarana Group. It teaches engineering, diplomas, management, computer applications, sciences, law, pharmacy and arts on one campus on the Rajkot-Morbi Road, and publishes a US-dollar fee sheet for international admissions.
universities.campusLifestyle: The single campus on the Rajkot-Morbi Road has 1.6 million sq ft of built-up space and 38 research labs. Ten of them are industry labs, including Wipro, Bosch and Google labs, CAD/CAM and a smart foundry. Marwadi reports 1,700+ international students from 54 countries, 500 faculty members and 120 PhD faculty. The library holds over 50,000 books, 60+ e-resources and 15+ Kindle e-readers. Sports facilities include outdoor grounds, a gym, a box cricket ground and indoor games, plus a lake with a jogging track.
universities.cityProfile: Marwadi University sits on the Rajkot-Morbi Highway, Rajkot 360003, in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat in western India. Marwadi describes Rajkot as a metropolitan area of more than 2 million people (2021). It calls the city a centre for diesel engines, submersible pumps, forging, ceramics and textiles. Mahatma Gandhi went to school here, at Alfred High School. The university arranges pickup from Rajkot Airport for a separate USD 15 fee, and helps students get local transport. Places nearby that Marwadi lists include the Mahatma Gandhi Museum and Watson Museum in the city, plus Girnar, Gir Forest National Park, Somnath, Dwarka and the Rann of Kutch.
universities.practicalExposure: The National Board of Accreditation's Tier I (Washington Accord) register lists five Marwadi B.Tech programmes. Civil and Mechanical Engineering are accredited to 30 June 2027. Chemical Engineering, Computer Engineering and Information & Communication Technology are accredited to 30 June 2028. The MBA is on NBA's Management PG register to 30 June 2027. Marwadi reports 38 research labs, including 10 industry labs such as Wipro, Bosch, Google, CAD/CAM and a smart foundry. It also has a high-performance computing facility awarded by GUJCOST (Government of Gujarat) and an IBM Innovation Center for Education programme. Marwadi says it was a partner of ISRO and ITCA for the launch of Gujarat's first student satellite in 2022. Its research consultancy has served more than 150 clients. It lists student and faculty exchanges with universities in the USA, Germany, Poland and other countries, and MoUs with Asia Pacific University (Malaysia) and the Inter American University of Puerto Rico. The B.Com (Hons) International Accounting is aligned with the ACCA qualification.
universities.hostelOverview: Marwadi's hostels house more than 4,500 students in separate blocks for men and women, each with wardens. The with-hostel international fee is a package. It covers a shared four-person non-AC room with bed, study table and wardrobe, plus meals, including three non-veg meals a week. International students live on an international floor with laundry, a TV room, a gym and indoor sports. When rooms run short, students may be placed off campus, with university transport at set times. On the B.Tech CSE, for example, the package is USD 3,200 a year against USD 2,000 without hostel. Hostel admission is renewed at the start of each academic year.
universities.dietarySupport: Marwadi runs a dedicated international canteen that serves international food, including non-vegetarian dishes. The with-hostel fee package includes meals, with three non-veg meals a week. The hostels have laundry and refrigerators, and on-campus catering serves meals through the day.
universities.safetyOverview: Marwadi reports 24/7 security staff and CCTV at campus doorways. A medical centre has a doctor during OPD hours, a pharmacy and a 24/7 ambulance. Men and women live in separate hostel blocks with wardens. The Student Section helps international students with FRRO registration after arrival.

faq.question: Is Marwadi University public or private?
faq.answer: It is a state private university. It was established under the Gujarat Private Universities Act No. 9 of 2016 on 9 May 2016 and is promoted by the Marwadi Chandarana Group. UGC lists it among Gujarat's state private universities, and UGC wrote to the university in March 2020 confirming its inclusion under Section 2(f) of the UGC Act, 1956.

faq.question: What language are programmes taught in?
faq.answer: English. Marwadi admits all its international students under the Government of India's Study in India programme, and Study in India states that English is the medium of instruction at its partner institutes. Marwadi also runs English language courses for international students who want to strengthen their communication skills.

faq.question: Do international applicants need an entrance exam or English test?
faq.answer: Marwadi's international route has no entrance-test stage. A country coordinator checks your mark sheets and issues an offer letter if you are eligible. GUJCET, ACPC counselling and CMAT belong to Gujarat's domestic admission route. Marwadi publishes no IELTS or TOEFL minimum, but teaching is in English.

faq.question: What are the academic entry requirements?
faq.answer: They vary by programme. Most B.Tech branches need Class 12 with Physics and Mathematics and 45-50 per cent. BBA and the integrated LL.B. degrees need 10+2 with 50 per cent. B.Pharm needs 45 per cent with Physics and Chemistry. Engineering diplomas are entered after Grade 10, Form 4 or O Level. Master's programmes need a relevant bachelor's degree; for example, the LL.M. needs 55 per cent in a law degree.

faq.question: How much does a year at Marwadi cost?
faq.answer: The 2026-27 international fee sheet lists yearly fees with and without hostel. For example: B.Tech CSE USD 2,000 (USD 3,200 with hostel), MBA USD 1,800 (USD 3,000), B.Pharm USD 2,300 (USD 3,500), and engineering diplomas USD 1,600 (USD 2,800). The hostel package includes a shared room and meals. Add USD 30 a semester for exams, USD 50 once for uniform, bag and ID card, USD 40 for convocation and USD 15 for an airport pickup.

faq.question: Are scholarships available?
faq.answer: Marwadi says it gives international students tuition scholarships of 45 to 100 per cent, depending on whether they take a hostel place. It says the fee sheet already shows fees after this scholarship. Its prospectus also names a fully funded President Scholarship through Study in India, for students with a hostel place. Students Traffic can help you confirm your scholarship terms in writing before you pay.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Register on the Study in India portal. Then send your mark sheets to Marwadi's country coordinator for your country: Grade 10 for diplomas, Grades 10 and 12 for bachelor's degrees, Grade 12 and bachelor's for master's. If you are eligible, you get an offer letter. Pay USD 500 of the admission fee, send the receipt with your details, and receive a confirmed admission letter before paying the rest of the semester fee.

faq.question: When does the academic year start?
faq.answer: Marwadi's most recent published calendar (2024-25) started semester I on 1 July 2024 for engineering, diploma, science, management, law, computer applications, pharmacy and arts programmes. The LL.M. runs in trimesters and began on 5 August 2024. The 2026-27 calendar had not been published when we checked, and there is no fixed international closing date.

faq.question: What is the accommodation like?
faq.answer: International students who take the hostel package share a four-person non-AC room with a bed, study table and wardrobe. They live on an international floor with laundry, a TV room, a gym and indoor sports. Meals are included, with three non-veg meals a week. When rooms run short, students may be housed off campus, with university transport at set times.

faq.question: Is Marwadi University accredited?
faq.answer: NAAC accredited Marwadi A+ (CGPA 3.31) in its first cycle, declared in November 2023. NBA's Tier I register lists five B.Tech programmes, and NBA also accredits the MBA. In NIRF 2025, Marwadi is in the 101-150 university band. The Bar Council of India approves its five-year BA LL.B. (Hons) and B.Com LL.B. (Hons) up to 2026-27. How your home country recognises the degree depends on its own rules.

faq.question: Does Marwadi pay for the flight to India?
faq.answer: Yes, for some students. Marwadi pays for the first flight only if you enrol on a course of three years or more and book a hostel place. If you later cancel your admission or the hostel, you pay back the flight. Students who choose not to live in the hostel do not get the free flight.

faq.question: What visa and registration rules apply?
faq.answer: You need an Indian student visa. If it is valid for more than 180 days, you must register with the FRRO within 14 days of arrival. Marwadi's Student Section helps with FRRO registration. Employment and business activity are not permitted on a student visa, so plan to fund your fees and living costs from outside India.

faq.question: Why are two fees listed for each programme?
faq.answer: Marwadi prices each programme two ways. The without-hostel figure is tuition only. The with-hostel figure is a package that adds a shared room, meals and, on courses of three years or more, the first flight. On most programmes the package adds USD 1,200 a year. That makes it simple to compare with renting privately in Rajkot.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.
